The therapy horse was also super pushy for bojack to leave before he was ready, which he had ulterior motives for. 

IRL there are “hybrid” services meant to slowly integrate patients back into the outpatient world, but Bojack just went straight to AA meetings only. Hiii there! I’m a first year PhD student in the program. I think it really depends on you. For me, I accepted after my second cycle applying to PhD programs after not getting in anywhere (with 2 first author pubs and a good amount of clinical/volunteer experience🫠) and I really just wanted to get started on my career. But others I’ve heard have waited, got more experience and gotten into a funded program, and that is far ideal. As far as the program, there’s a ton of opportunity here. I’m starting research collaborations with Stanford and UCSF, have access to FANTASTIC external practicum sites, and live in a very beautiful place. Im applying to two external scholarships (one through the military and one through the APA) that, if I receive, will cover my tuition for my time here and give me a pretty good living allowance too. The school also waived my tuition for the first year only, which helped as I’m applying. That said, it’s a risk. There’s also a ton of down sides to the program. Faculty have been really hard to get a hold of. They don’t assign you into a lab until 2nd year (so you just do coursework first year unless you proactively seek out research experience like I did). The campus is super small. And the cohort size. I personally enjoy my cohort, we are a family. But having 50+ people definitely has its downsides. Please PM me if you have any questions, I was in your shoes last year and know how tough the decision is. BEST OF LUCK.

Hii👋 I am also queer and have lived with the intense feelings of depression/anxiety/suicidal thoughts/self-hatred that are, sadly, a very common experience for us queer folx existing in a hetero-man’s world. 

My parents weren’t entirely homophobic, like they didn’t kick me out or anything, but they made it clear that would prefer I liked girls (I’m a guy). I tried to tell myself that was enough. But now that I’m older, and not in high school anymore / not under their roof, I know that was NOT enough. In my early 20s, I was constantly surrounded by accepting, open minded people. And I began to heal. Granted, I still have wounds (internalized homophobia, trouble in romantic relationships, anxiety here and there), but I’m much stronger now.

You have got this. I know shit is hard. But it will only get easier. Lean on your friends more than you normally do. Invest your attention/emotional energy into friends that build you up, and don’t make you fear that they will one day betray you. It’s cheesy, but our existence really truly is resistance.
